s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk in a patient with a history of systemic sclerosis
salient_findings: Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
Nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles on lesional punch biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis
Patient has tried treating the rash with topical aloe without improvement
Review of systems is negative for new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Patient has a history of heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
Patient is receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Complete blood cell count with differential is unremarkable
Tissue cultures are negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus
Lesional punch biopsy specimens show nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles

shortlist.label: bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash and firm, red-brown plaques

shortlist.label: dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash and history of systemic sclerosis

shortlist.label: eczema
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash and lack of response to topical aloe

shortlist.label: urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash and presence of firm, red-brown plaques

shortlist.label: dermatitis herpetiformis
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic rash and history of systemic sclerosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, and the lack of response to topical aloe, is most consistent with dermatitis. The histopathological findings of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The patient's rash does not have the characteristic bullae or blisters of bullous pemphigoid

rejected.label: eczema
rejected.why: While eczema is a type of dermatitis, the patient's presentation and histopathological findings are more consistent with a broader diagnosis of dermatitis

rejected.label: urticaria
rejected.why: The patient's rash is not described as having the characteristic wheals or hives of urticaria

rejected.label: dermatitis herpetiformis
rejected.why: The patient's rash does not have the characteristic vesicles or blisters of dermatitis herpetiformis, and the histopathological findings do not support this diagnosis
